cards.sig: for me it was czech. it's really close to russian, but it's a lot harder than you'd think. чешский похож на русский — казалось, будет легко for me it was czech. i thought it's easy to learn a language which is similar. think a language, a city or a job that was harder than you'd think. why? harder than you'd think = what anyone expects vs reality. about your own past expectation: i thought it would be easy. «сложнее, чем кажется»

communication with non-technical managers — it's a lot harder than you'd think. чему учишься на работе: говорить с менеджерами без технического бэкграунда communication with non-technical managers — it's harder than i was thinking. one thing at work or at home that's a lot harder than you'd think. than i was thinking is a calque. anyone would think so → than you'd think; only you → than i thought. калька с «чем я думала»

i picked up how to manage staff on the job, from my general managers. university only gets you so far. управлять людьми учишься у своих руководителей i picked up how to manage staff on the job, from my general managers. you can't learn it at uni. far [my degree · school · a course] only got me so far — i picked up [people skills · most of the software · the local language] on the job. you can't learn it at university is correct. the box phrase says more: university gives you the basics, the rest comes on the job. вуз даёт базу — дальше на работе · staff /stɑːf/ (ame /stæf/) — персонал · stuff /stʌf/ — вещи

i realised that university only gets you so far, so i found a full-time job. зачем работать на полный день, ещё учась в вузе i understood that just studying at university isn't enough for me, so i found a full-time job. your degree or your school — where did it only get you so far? understood → realised (it became clear to you); isn't enough for me → only gets you so far. осознала · даёт базу — и не больше

ai helps me make suggestions, but choosing the best one — that's where i really add value. когда пишешь код вместе с ии ai helps me make suggestions, but finally i choose the best one with my own experience. value in your work or your life now, where do you really add value? finally in mid-sentence sounds like «наконец-то»; «в итоге» is in the end. add value = what you bring that ai can't. «вот где от меня польза»

networking, department heads, motivation — that's where people still add value. что остаётся за топ-менеджерами, когда ии есть на всех уровнях networking, department heads, motivation — in this kind of area, i believe ai is still helpless. [calming down an angry client · breaking bad news to a client · negotiating a good deal · noticing when a colleague is struggling] — that's where people still add value. ai can …, but … helpless is usually about people. the box phrase talks about what people do well, not what ai can't do. helpless — «беспомощный», обычно о людях

top managers still work with paper documents — they could go to jail. that's why we don't hand anything serious over to ai. почему серьёзные документы не доверяют ии top managers still work with paper documents — they could go to jail. that's why we don't use ai for serious work. hand one thing you'd never hand over to ai. why not? hand sth over to ai = give ai the whole job, not just use it. «передать ии целиком»

things that took me five hours a couple of years ago, i now hand over to ai — it does them in five minutes. что ии теперь делает за тебя на работе things that took me five hours a couple of years ago, ai could do for five minutes. one task you've handed over to ai — or would love to. emails? meeting notes? translations? planning a trip? in five minutes = how long it takes to finish; for five minutes = how long it goes on. «за пять минут» — in five minutes

this is touch typing. it comes in really handy. что пригодилось из того, чему учились сами this is touch typing. and it's very useful for typing. handy [touch typing · knowing a bit of the local language · my first-aid course · excel · being able to drive] came in really handy when i … very useful for typing repeats typing; it comes in handy = it turns out to be useful. touch typing, not blind typing. «пригождается» · слепая печать — touch typing

children just go home, ask ai and write it down. so what's the point of homework? о домашке, когда есть ии children just go home, ask ai and write it down. it's useless at all. point so what's the point of [team-building days · performance reviews · homework for young kids · learning poems by heart]? does your partner agree? why (not)? at all goes with not and questions (not useful at all). what's the point of…? = «какой смысл в…?» «какой смысл в…?»

what's the point of learning to code? a lot of tech companies have stopped hiring juniors. they're handing all that work over to ai. whatever we learn now will be out of date by the time we graduate from university. finn, 17, student. wants to cut coding.

i don't need people who know a particular booking system: it'll be out of date in two years. they need to adapt. i need people who can read up on something new and teach themselves. omar, 52, a parent. runs a group of small hotels and does the hiring. wants to add “how to learn”.

nobody prepared us for angry customers. i had to learn the hard way. and it would have been so easy to teach: two or three role-plays in class. chloe, 24, a former student. her first job was in a call centre. wants to add “dealing with difficult people”.
it's a lot harder than you'd think — i couldn't walk the next day. yoga? isn't that just stretching? hard
it's a lot steeper than you'd think — take water. the walk up to the castle? it can't be far, can it? steep
they're a lot friendlier than you'd think — they fed our cat all summer. your neighbours? they look a bit grumpy. friendly
he's on it more often than you'd think — mostly sending me memes. your dad has a smartphone? does he ever actually use it? often

for me it was czech. it's really close to russian, but it's a lot harder than you'd think. чешский похож на русский — казалось, будет легко for me it was czech. i thought it's easy to learn a language which is similar. think [learning the local language · moving to a new country · getting used to retirement · raising a teenager · starting my own business] was / is a lot harder than you'd think. i thought it would be …, but … harder than you'd think = what anyone expects vs reality. about your own past expectation: i thought it would be easy. «сложнее, чем кажется»

communication with non-technical managers — it's a lot harder than you'd think. чему учишься на работе: говорить с менеджерами без технического бэкграунда communication with non-technical managers — it's harder than i was thinking. [explaining my job to my parents · switching off after work · making friends as an adult · getting a teenager to tell you about their day · filling your days after you retire] is a lot harder than you'd think — especially when … than i was thinking is a calque. anyone would think so → than you'd think; only you → than i thought. калька с «чем я думала»

i realised that university only gets you so far, so i found a full-time job. зачем работать на полный день, ещё учась в вузе i understood that just studying at university isn't enough for me, so i found a full-time job. when i [became a parent · moved abroad · got my first job · started managing people · retired], i realised that [a degree · school english · reading parenting books · training] only gets you so far. understood → realised (it became clear to you); isn't enough for me → only gets you so far. осознала · даёт базу — и не больше

ai helps me make suggestions, but choosing the best one — that's where i really add value. когда пишешь код вместе с ии ai helps me make suggestions, but finally i choose the best one with my own experience. value [ai writes the first draft · an app finds the cheapest flights · a junior analyst crunches the numbers], but [checking it · knowing which places my family will actually enjoy · explaining what the numbers mean to the client] — that's where i really add value. finally in mid-sentence sounds like «наконец-то»; «в итоге» is in the end. add value = what you bring that ai can't. «вот где от меня польза»
it's been ages! how have you been? at a wedding you see an old friend at a wedding. «сто лет не виделись! как ты?»
last i heard, you were moving to montreal! montreal «последнее, что я слышала, — ты переезжал в монреаль!»
so how are you finding it (so far)? a new city they moved to a new city a month ago. «ну и как тебе там?»
i've been meaning to get in touch for ages! a message «я сто лет собиралась тебе написать!»
so, what have you been up to? your news «ну, рассказывай, чем занимался?»
oh, this and that. i've taken up climbing, actually! nothing special your friend asks what you've been up to. «да так, то одно, то другое…» + one real detail
still at the bank? — still at the bank! the bank you remember he worked at a bank. «ты всё ещё в банке?» — «всё там же!»
that must keep you busy! three kids your friend has three kids and a new job. «скучать некогда!»
it was lovely to catch up with everyone! after the party the day after a reunion, a message to the group: «было так здорово со всеми повидаться!»
